issue_context.title: [API Proposal]: File.AppendAllBytes
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-io See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
### Background and motivation The File class has all methods for bytes which also exist for text except of appending data. Not only that it fits into the api surface by filling this gap is also saves us writing more than one line of code. ### API Proposal ```csharp namespace System.Collections.Generic; public class System.IO { public static void AppendAllBytes(string path, byte[]? data) } ``` ### API Usage ```csharp byte[] data = File.ReadAllBytes("C:\\1.bin"); File.AppendAllBytes("C:\\2.bin", data); ``` ### Alternative Designs _No response_ ### Risks _No response_
Author: Symbai
Assignees: -
Labels: `api-suggestion`, `area-System.IO`, `untriaged`
Milestone: -
The `data` argument should be of type `ReadOnlySpan<byte>` instead of `byte[]?`?

> The `data` argument should be of type `ReadOnlySpan<byte>` instead of `byte[]?`?

`WriteAllBytes` [uses byte[]](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/210a7a9feec64b7fac5147656cddb199ec90cf75/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/IO/File.cs#L683) instead of span, thats why I used it here as well but yeah sure it can be a span.

> * Why the API should allow for `null`s? What is the point of appending nothing to a file?

The AppendAllText allows a nullable string I only followed this choice.

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/4c75b589338320ab38a93567587cdb1535d9de0d/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/IO/File.cs#L775-L776

Possibly because of that:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/4c75b589338320ab38a93567587cdb1535d9de0d/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/IO/File.cs#L1211-L1222

> Why the API should allow for nulls? What is the point of appending nothing to a file? Creating it? If so, we have dedicated API for that.

There's value in being consistent with the existing APIs here.  If someone is using WriteAllText with something that ends up being null and they decide to switch to appending rather than overriding, it'd be nice if that didn't then entail having to handle the arguments differently.

> The mentioned APIs were introduced before Span and Memory, the new methods should accepts ReadOnlySpan and ReadOnlyMemory to accept both arrays and other types of inputs.

Do we want `ReadOnly{Span/Memory}<byte>` overloads then for the existing ones?  What about `ReadOnlySpan<char>` for the ones currently only accepting strings?

> Do we want ReadOnly{Span/Memory}<byte> overloads then for the existing ones? What about ReadOnlySpan<char> for the ones currently only accepting strings?

I would not mind adding them, but I would prefer to see an actual need first (otherwise we should do it for all existing APIs that accept only arrays).

Here are some tips for contributor who want to take this issue:

- before you start working on it, please let me know so I can assign you and nobody else is going to work on it at the same time and duplicate the effort
- [here](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/workflow/README.md) you can find our workflow instructions, the first step is to install everything required to build the product
- to build the clr, libs and tests you need to build following subsets:
```cmd
.\build.cmd -c Release -subset clr+libs+libs.tests
```
- the `File` type is included in corelib, not in `System.IO.dll`: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/IO/File.cs
- its tests are in `System.IO.FileSystem`: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/tree/main/src/libraries/System.IO.FileSystem/tests/File
- the test projects can access only the public classes and methods that were added to the ref assembly: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/104752ae2874cc6a1d4ff709f0dfaae0c7e06931/src/libraries/System.Runtime/ref/System.Runtime.cs#L9544
- To rebuild only the corelib (where File class is) and run the tests you can run following command:
```cmd
.\build.cmd -c Release -subset clr.corelib+clr.nativecorelib+libs.PreTest && .\dotnet.cmd build -c Release .\src\libraries\System.IO.FileSystem\System.IO.FileSystem.sln && .\dotnet.cmd build -c Release .\src\libraries\System.IO.FileSystem\tests\System.IO.FileSystem.Tests.csproj /t:Test
```
